gloss: to charge; to make an in-app purchase

definitions.gloss: to charge a fee; to impose a charge
definitions.explanation: For a service provider to charge users a fee for services or content.

definitions.gloss: to make an in-app purchase; to pay for digital content
definitions.explanation: In colloquial modern usage, to spend money on in-app purchases, microtransactions in games, or premium digital services. This sense reverses the original subject — the payer is the one who 課金する.

examples.japanese: {月額|げつがく}{課金|かきん}のサービスだ。
examples.english: It's a service with a monthly charge.

examples.japanese: {利用者|りようしゃ}に{課金|かきん}する{仕組|しく}みになっている。
examples.english: The system is set up to charge users.

examples.japanese: このアプリは{無料|むりょう}だが、{追加機能|ついかきのう}は{課金|かきん}が{必要|ひつよう}だ。
examples.english: This app is free, but additional features require payment.

examples.japanese: ゲームに{課金|かきん}しすぎた。
examples.english: I spent too much on in-game purchases.

examples.japanese: {課金|かきん}しないと{強|つよ}くなれない。
examples.english: You can't get stronger without paying.

examples.japanese: {毎月|まいつき}ソシャゲに{何万円|なんまんえん}も{課金|かきん}している{友人|ゆうじん}がいる。
examples.english: I have a friend who spends tens of thousands of yen per month on mobile games.

notes:
Originally, {課金|かきん}する meant "to impose a charge" (the provider charges the user). In modern colloquial usage, especially in gaming and app culture, the meaning has shifted so that the user is the one who {課金|かきん}する (to pay/spend money). This semantic shift is widely recognized but sometimes criticized by language purists.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {課金|かきん}アイテム: paid item, purchasable item
- {課金|かきん}ユーザー: paying user
- {無課金|むかきん}: free-to-play (not spending money)
- {重課金|じゅうかきん}: heavy spending (on games)
- {微課金|びかきん}: light spending (small purchases)
- {廃課金|はいかきん}: extreme spending (whale)

USAGE:
The colloquial sense (sense 2) is dominant in everyday conversation, especially among younger speakers. Common in discussions about mobile games (ソシャゲ), streaming subscriptions, and app ecosystems.
